text:
My birds whisper three things this dawn.

Gandalf (1), your brazier burned steady while you weighed the miller’s grain—steady hands keep the flour clean.

Hermione (2) and Neo (6), my birds caught you trading a look when Yoda (3) passed—long enough to raise a question, short enough to vanish when questioned.

Batman (4), your boots left faint prints near the butcher’s stall before the first light; the butcher’s cat marked them twice.

*Dips quill, waits for the village to stir.*

Elsa (7): My birds add another whisper to the morning’s brood.

Sherlock (10), your question to Gandalf (1) echoes the bazaar’s own suspicion—yet the flock that distrusts the first voice often forgets that the first voice may only wish the scales balanced before the spice rots. Hermione (2), your tapestry metaphor holds a thread too tight; if the loom is half-awakened, who is pulling which strings?

Neo (6), your “empty loom” is a silence I share—yet a bazaar without voices is one where the hungriest merchants speak loudest. Ripley (5), your spice that lingers long may sweeten or spoil; the bazaar remembers the last merchant who sold yesterday’s rot as tomorrow’s promise.

Gandalf (1), your steady brazier still glows; may it light the path before the shadows grow.

*Dips quill, listens.*
